approach: Revision of round 1: the design is unchanged; only the criterion 5 demonstration was refused, so it now names its seam and what fails without the behavior. The change: in `crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs`, `event_of_job` passes the job's stored `candidate.producer_report` to `failure_details`. For a failed verification with unmet criteria, `failure_details` adds one block after the unmet list. For each unmet criterion (at most DETAIL_CAP, text clipped to TEXT_CAP) the block shows the producer's stored status and evidence from `criteria_check`, matched by the existing `criterion_key` normalisation. An unmatched criterion gets "no pre-verdict check recorded". A job with no candidate or no report gets one line saying so. A passing verification, a missing verification, and a failed verdict with no unmet criterion add nothing, so existing exact-text tests stay valid. `criterion_key` moves from `run/send_back.rs` into `introspect.rs` as `pub(crate)`. `send_back.rs` imports it, because `mod send_back;` is private to `run` (run/mod.rs:71) and `run/mod.rs` is not a deliverable. The CHANGELOG gets one entry in `### Fixed` naming the root cause.

decisions.choice: Move `criterion_key` (body and doc unchanged) from run/send_back.rs:359-380 into introspect.rs as `pub(crate)`; send_back.rs gets `use crate::introspect::criterion_key;`.
decisions.reason: The brief says to reuse the send-back normalisation. `send_back` is a private module of `run` (run/mod.rs:71), so `introspect.rs` cannot name `crate::run::send_back::criterion_key`, and `run/mod.rs` is not a deliverable. `pub mod introspect` is declared at lib.rs:126, so the send-back can reach `crate::introspect::criterion_key`. One definition means the two matchers cannot drift, and send_back.rs (a listed deliverable) gets a real edit, so it is not an unchanged deliverable.

rejected.why: introspect still cannot name the private `send_back` module, and re-exporting it needs an edit to run/mod.rs, which is not a deliverable.

rejected.option: Write a second trim/lowercase compare in introspect.rs
rejected.why: It would disagree with the send-back on `1.` prefixes, `[kind]` tags and trailing punctuation; the cosmetic variants in run_pin_tests.rs:1076-1099 show the normalisation producers rely on.
run/mod.rs is outside the listed deliverables.

decisions.choice: Add the pre-verdict block inside `failure_details` (new parameter `report: Option<&ProducerReport>`) only when the unmet list is non-empty; with no candidate or no report, add one line stating that no pre-verdict check was recorded.
decisions.reason: Criteria 1 and 3 conflict on the no-candidate case: criterion 1 says nothing is added when no candidate or report is stored, criterion 3 requires `what` to state that no pre-verdict check was recorded. I follow criterion 3, the specific behavior criterion, and read criterion 1 as: no producer status or evidence is ever invented. The stage must be able to tell an absent check from one nobody looked up, which is the original fault. The single caller of `failure_details` is introspect.rs:1499, so no other caller changes.

rejected.option: Add nothing when no candidate or report is stored
rejected.why: Contradicts criterion 3 and repeats the fault: silence is indistinguishable from the check not being looked up.

rejected.option: Add the block to every failed verdict, including one with no unmet criterion
rejected.why: The existing early return at introspect.rs:1006-1010 and tests at 2794-2802 pin the 'lists no unmet criterion' text; the producer's check of criteria is only relevant when a criterion is unmet.

decisions.choice: Show only the producer's status and evidence for each unmet criterion; not the report's summary, checks_run, mistakes or desires.
decisions.reason: `ReportedCriterion {criterion, status, evidence}` (athena-data/src/records.rs:806-810) is exactly the producer's own check against one criterion. The report is stored redacted (records.rs:812), so the text is safe to carry. Counts and text are capped with DETAIL_CAP (introspect.rs:945) and `clip(.., TEXT_CAP)` (introspect.rs:947, 952). Empty evidence is shown as 'no evidence given'.

rejected.why: It adds size and unrelated text; the other fields are not evidence about the unmet criterion.

decisions.choice: Use one constant phrase, `no pre-verdict check recorded`, for both the unmatched-criterion line and the no-report line, and keep the heading free of the exact phrases 'Unmet acceptance criteria' and 'Failed checks'.
decisions.reason: Existing tests assert `!what.contains("Failed checks")` (introspect.rs:2744, athena-cli/tests/introspection.rs:470) and `!what.contains("Unmet acceptance criteria")` (introspect.rs:2763). One phrase keeps the new tests' asserts consistent in case.

rejected.option: Reword the existing headings or add the block under the unmet heading
rejected.why: Would risk the existing exact-phrase assertions for no gain.

rejected.why: That was the prior job's misreading; the introspection stage never reads the invocation detail.

risks.risk: Criteria 1 and 3 conflict on a job with no stored candidate (nothing added, versus a statement that no check was recorded).
risks.mitigation: The plan follows criterion 3, the specific behavior criterion, and reads criterion 1 as 'no producer status or evidence is invented'. The only text added for a job with no candidate is the 'no pre-verdict check recorded' line. A verdict with no unmet criterion, a passing one and a missing one add nothing. The CHANGELOG entry says so. This resolution was in the round 1 plan and the critic did not contest it.

risks.risk: The producer's criterion text differs from the verifier's, so the match fails and the stage is told the check was not recorded.
risks.mitigation: The match uses `criterion_key`, the normalisation the send-back already uses (prefix, `[kind]` tag, case, spacing and trailing punctuation ignored). The criterion 2 test includes a prefixed and punctuated variant. A genuinely reworded criterion shows as 'no pre-verdict check recorded', and the CHANGELOG states this limit.

risks.risk: Moving `criterion_key` into introspect.rs puts a send-back helper in a module with a different purpose, and send_back.rs now depends on introspect.
risks.mitigation: The dependency is inside one crate, the function is pure, and `crate::introspect` is already imported by other modules (proposals.rs:22, scope_guard.rs:34, labeled.rs:32). The doc comment says the function is shared. Moving it to a neutral module would mean editing run/mod.rs or lib.rs, which are not deliverables; the CHANGELOG notes it as a follow-up.

risks.risk: A clippy `-D warnings` or fmt failure, for example a redundant import or an unused function.
risks.mitigation: The new tests import only `Candidate` and `ReportedCriterion` explicitly in the test module (`ProducerReport` arrives through `use super::*`), the helper names (`candidate_with`, `producer_report`) do not clash with `criterion`, `check`, `finding` or `verification`, and the producer runs `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` before finishing. `rustfmt` orders the new `use` line in send_back.rs.

risks.risk: A job's candidate record may not be at HEAD when the introspection reads it, so a real stored check shows as absent.
risks.mitigation: The introspection event is built from the stored candidate at HEAD of the records read by `GitRecords::load` (introspect.rs:1474). Candidate files are written under `<job dir>/candidate.json` with the verification (records.rs:1326-1329), and lifecycle.rs:92 reads them at HEAD. When the file is missing the output is the no-candidate line, which is the stated behavior.
